1.title: Value Stream Mapping and Management
1.text: Welcome to Module twelve: Value Stream Mapping and Management. It covers the exam area Value stream identification, mapping and management. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Define value stream, core value stream, enabling value stream, value stream mapping, value stream management and complexity thinking. Understand the difference between core and enabling streams. Understand how workflows are optimized for complexity. Know the purpose of mapping and management, their relationship, and the elements of a value stream map. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Value stream identification, mapping and management (five percent). Exam format: forty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; twenty-six correct answers (sixty-five percent) pass. Validated against: the official eye til Foundation (Version five) syllabus, version five point zero (February two thousand twenty-six).

1.title: Value streams
1.text: Value streams. A value stream is the series of steps an organization takes to create and deliver products and services to consumers: from demand to value. Core value stream. Meaning: Delivers value directly to a consumer. Example: Handling a customer order from request to delivery. Enabling value stream. Meaning: Supports the core streams inside the organization. Example: Hiring, finance, supplier management, tooling. Exam tip: Core equals the consumer feels it. Enabling equals it helps the core streams work.

1.title: Value stream mapping and management
1.text: Value stream mapping and management. Value stream mapping (V S M). Drawing the steps, flows and waits of a value stream to see how work really moves. Value stream management (V S M). Continuously managing and improving value streams using what the map shows. Purpose: to find waste, delay and handoffs, agree where to improve, and improve flow and value. Relationship: mapping shows, management improves. The map is the tool; management is the ongoing discipline that uses it.

1.title: Elements of a value stream map
1.text: Elements of a value stream map. The figure shows this: A value stream map: steps, flow, wait times and handoffs.

1.title: Elements of a value stream map, continued
1.text: Elements of a value stream map. Steps or activities. The work done at each stage. Flow and handoffs. Where work moves from one team or tool to another. Time. Process time (working) and wait time (queueing). Roles and tools. Who and what is involved. Information flow. How demand and data travel. Waste and problems. Delays, rework, defects to fix. Exact element names may differ in the official book; the idea is to visualize steps, flow and time.

1.title: Complexity thinking
1.text: Complexity thinking. Complexity thinking recognizes that many situations are complex: cause and effect cannot be fully predicted, parts interact, and change creates surprises. Workflows are therefore optimized for complexity with short cycles, experiments, feedback, autonomy for teams and learning, instead of rigid, fully planned processes. It links to progress iteratively with feedback and voo ka (volatile, uncertain, complex and ambiguous) (Module three). Exam tip: Complex equals unpredictable, so probe, learn and adapt. Complicated equals knowable with expertise. eye til pushes iteration and feedback when work is complex. Exam tip: Mapping draws the stream; management improves it. If a question asks who benefits directly, core streams reach consumers and enabling streams support them.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Which value stream delivers value directly to consumers? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Core value stream. A core value stream delivers value directly.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A mapping workshop shows an order waits five days between two teams. What is the likely next step? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Improve the handoff, using value stream management. The map reveals delay, and management improves it.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which statements about value stream mapping and management are C O R R E C T? (one) Mapping visualizes how work moves. (two) Management continuously improves value streams. (three) Mapping is an ongoing management discipline that replaces management. (four) A map shows only the final result and ignores wait time. The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: one and two. Mapping visualizes, management improves.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Identify the missing word(s). A(n) blank value stream supports the core value streams inside the organization. The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Enabling. Enabling value streams support the core ones.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Work is unpredictable and parts interact in surprising ways. Which approach does complexity thinking favor? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Short cycles, experiments and feedback. Complex work calls for iteration and learning.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Hiring and finance processes keep the organization running but are not seen by consumers. Which type of stream are they? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Enabling. They support the core streams.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Define a value stream. Answer: The series of steps an organization takes to create and deliver products and services. Question two. What is the difference between core and enabling value streams? Answer: Core delivers value directly to consumers; enabling supports the core streams. Question three. What does value stream mapping do? Answer: Visualizes the steps, flow and waits of a value stream.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does value stream management do? Answer: Continuously manages and improves value streams. Question five. What is complexity thinking? Answer: Recognizing that cause and effect are not fully predictable and working with iteration and feedback. Question six. Name two things a value stream map shows. Answer: Steps and handoffs, and process and wait time.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Value stream: steps from demand to value. Core or enabling: consumer feels it or supports the core. Mapping or management: shows the flow or improves it. Map elements: steps, flow, time, roles, information, waste. Complexity thinking: unpredictable; iterate with feedback.
